issue_text: I need the full details for my round-trip airline reservation C4C633. Please give me the complete itinerary, both passengers currently on the booking, how many bags are already attached, whether insurance is included, and the payment history. Also, while you’re in that reservation, check the current status of outbound flight FLE7F420 for 2026-10-01 and tell me whether that segment still looks normal.
summary: A long multi-domain concierge session for one user. It starts in the tau2Airline system: the agent loads the airline skill, recovers from a data-model error by querying the database directly, and reports full C4C633 details (itinerary, passengers, bags, Standard insurance, $70 payment) plus the status of the outbound segment. It then runs a confirm-before-mutate loop for three airline changes — adding a middle name to passenger 1, a requested flight update it correctly identifies as a no-op (the flights already match), and adding one $50 checked bag — followed by a read-only EC4C1C lookup. The session then switches skills to send an SMS to Jordan Kim, and finally loads the retail skill to authenticate the user, search in-stock electronics, and process a confirmed order return/refund. The outcome is recorded unresolved: two past-dated flight segments (Oct 1 and Sep 16, both before the stated 'today' of Oct 22) are reported as 'normal' without flagging that they already departed, and the requested middle name is folded into the first-name field.

findings.title: Past-dated flights reported as 'normal'
findings.body: The C4C633 outbound segment (2026-10-01) and the EC4C1C flight (2026-09-16) both predate the stated 'today' of Oct 22, 2026, yet the agent reports each as showing 'no delays or cancellations — everything looks normal' without noting the segment already flew.

findings.title: Middle name stored in the first-name field
findings.body: The user asked to add Maya's middle name 'Lin'. The agent confirms it as a middle-name addition but the executed change updates passenger 1's first name from 'Maya' to 'Maya Lin', so the stored structure doesn't match the requested semantics.

findings.title: Good confirm-before-mutate discipline and clean recovery
findings.body: After the initial data-model error the agent works around it via direct DB access, correctly flags the identical-flights update as a no-op rather than issuing a pointless write, and gates every mutation (name change, extra bag, retail return) behind an explicit yes/no confirmation.
